children: New attacks sent oil above $90 just as Kevin Warsh revived rate-hike fears. Monday has declined the market’s request for a quiet start.
Futures end August cautiously

S&P 500 futures slipped around 0.3% Monday, while Nasdaq contracts dropped 0.5%. European futures also weakened and Asian equities fell as renewed US-Iran fighting lifted oil prices and kept Treasury yields elevated.
Wall Street ended Friday lower after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the central bank’s commitment to fighting inflation.
The S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,711.76, the Nasdaq lost 0.52% to 26,402.42 and the Dow closed nearly flat at 53,559.99.
Despite Friday’s pullback, the major indexes finished the week higher after
and
, CrowdStrike and Okta earnings revived the AI trade.
Oil adds fresh inflation pressure

Brent crude surged roughly 2.8% to $90.60 this morning, while WTI gained 2.5% after US forces attacked Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island. Iran retaliated against American forces in Jordan, abruptly interrupting last week’s optimism around reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
President Trump said Iran’s Kharg Island oil terminal was being heavily bombed, although the US military had not confirmed the claim.
Kharg handles most Iranian crude exports, meaning verified damage could create a physical supply disruption rather than another temporary geopolitical premium.
Higher oil complicates the inflation outlook by raising transportation, manufacturing and consumer costs. It also pressures technology valuations through the bond market.
Persistent inflation supports higher yields, and higher yields reduce the present value of companies whose largest profits are expected somewhere in the future.
Warsh leaves traders hawkish
Markets now price roughly a 57% probability of a September rate increase, up sharply after Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech.
The two-year Treasury yield climbed toward 4.33%, its highest in a month. Apparently, “data dependent” currently translates to “bring us softer data quickly.”

The dollar index held near a two-week high around 99.60, while USD/JPY climbed above ¥160 and revived intervention risk. Gold dropped toward $4,450, silver retreated below $67 and Bitcoin traded near $77,000 as higher yields weakened demand for non-yielding and alternative assets.
Friday’s US employment report is the week’s main scheduled test. Economists expect payrolls to rebound by roughly 58,000 after July’s surprise 23,000 decline, with unemployment holding at 4.1%.
Stronger hiring could solidify a September hike; another weak report may reopen the debate almost immediately.
